source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 26 (PDF 145-159, printed 142-156); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 26 (Polymers), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The small molecules that join together to make a polymer are called:
blocks.explanation: Polymers are very large molecules made by joining many small molecules called monomers through polymerisation (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Polymers are very large molecules made by joining many small molecules called monomers through polymerisation.

blocks.prompt: 2 Which polymer does the chapter name for making clothesline?
blocks.explanation: Shopping bags are made of poly(ethene) and clothesline of poly(propene) (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: from shopping bags (poly(ethene)) and clothesline (poly(propene))

blocks.prompt: 3 Kevlar® is suitable for bulletproof vests because it is:

options.text: a very light and soft material

blocks.explanation: Poly(ethene) and poly(propene) are very light and soft, whereas Kevlar® is a hard material suitable for bulletproof vests (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: whereas Kevlar® is a hard material suitable for bulletproof vests

blocks.prompt: 4 According to the chapter, the properties of polymers depend on:

options.text: only the colour of the monomers
the type and number of monomers and the method of manufacture
only the number of hydrogen atoms

blocks.explanation: The properties of polymers vary with the type and number of monomers in the polymer and the method through which they are manufactured (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: The properties of polymers broadly vary depending on the type and number of monomers in the polymer

blocks.prompt: 5 The systematic name of polythene is:
blocks.explanation: Synthetic polymers are named by writing 'poly' before the monomer's name, so polythene is poly(ethene) (Keep in Mind).

book_ref.quote: polythene is systematically named as poly(ethene)

blocks.prompt: 6 Polyvinylchloride is systematically named:
blocks.explanation: Its monomer is chloroethene, so polyvinylchloride is called poly(chloroethene) (Keep in Mind).

book_ref.quote: polyvinylchloride is called poly(chloroethene)

blocks.prompt: 7 For polymers made from two or more monomers, common names are usually used because:

options.text: the systematic name is too long

blocks.explanation: For polymers with two or more monomers the systematic name is too long, so common names are used (Keep in Mind).

book_ref.quote: common names are usually used because the systematic name is too long

blocks.prompt: 8 Poly(ethane-1,2-diyl benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate) is commonly called:
blocks.explanation: Its systematic name is too long, so it is commonly called polyethylene terephthalate, PETE (Keep in Mind).

book_ref.quote: This is why poly(ethane-1,2-diyl benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate) is commonly called polyethylene terephthalate, i.e. PETE.

blocks.prompt: 9 The two main types of polymerisation are:
blocks.explanation: Polymerisation is the joining of monomers to form a polymer; its two main types are addition and condensation polymerisation (26.1).

book_ref.quote: Polymerisation is the process of joining monomers to form a polymer.

blocks.prompt: 10 In addition polymerisation:

options.text: a water molecule is lost at each link
half of the atoms are lost as gas
a small molecule is always produced
all the atoms of the monomers become part of the polymer

blocks.explanation: In addition polymerisation monomers add one by one and all the atoms of the original monomers become part of the polymer; nothing is lost (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: All the atoms from the original monomers become part of the polymer.

blocks.prompt: 11 A monomer for addition polymerisation must contain:
blocks.explanation: Monomers must have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, which opens up to let the monomers link (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Monomers must have a carbon-carbon double (C=C) or triple bond (C≡C).

blocks.prompt: 12 Addition polymerisation often takes place as a chain reaction started by:

options.text: an initiator that forms free radicals
a dehydrating agent that removes water

blocks.explanation: The chain reaction is started by a very reactive molecule, an initiator, which forms free radicals (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: an initiator, which forms free radicals

blocks.prompt: 13 In the formation of poly(ethene), ethene molecules join by:

options.text: breaking double bonds and linking end-to-end

blocks.explanation: A large number of ethene (CH₂=CH₂) molecules add together by breaking double bonds and linking end-to-end (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: add together by breaking double bonds and linking end-to-end

blocks.prompt: 14 Light shopping bags and light plastic bottles are made of:
blocks.explanation: Low density poly(ethene) is used where a very light and soft material is needed, such as shopping bags and light plastic bottles (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Low density poly(ethene) is used where a very light and soft material is needed

blocks.prompt: 15 HDPE is produced from ethene using:

options.text: Ziegler-Natta catalyst at low pressure and temperature
a free radical initiator at very high pressure

blocks.explanation: HDPE is produced from ethene with the Ziegler-Natta catalyst at low pressure and temperature (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: HDPE is produced from ethene using a catalyst called

blocks.prompt: 16 LDPE is a less solid and more elastic material than HDPE because its chains are:

options.text: more branched and cannot pack tightly

blocks.explanation: LDPE chains are more branched, so they are unable to pack tightly, giving a less solid and more elastic material (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: LDPE and HDPE differ in the nature of their chains with LDPE being more branched.

blocks.prompt: 17 HDPE is a tough and dense material because:

options.text: its linear chains pack closely to give a compact structure

blocks.explanation: HDPE has linear chains that pack closely to give a compact structure, a tough and dense material (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: While HDPE has linear chains allowing them to pack closely

blocks.prompt: 18 The Ziegler-Natta catalyst was first discovered by Karl Ziegler in:
blocks.explanation: It was initially discovered by Karl Ziegler in 1953 and allowed low-pressure polymerisation of ethene into HDPE (Did You Know?, 26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: It was initially discovered by Karl Ziegler in 1953.

blocks.prompt: 19 Giulio Natta used the same catalyst family to make:

options.text: stereoregular polymers such as crystalline polypropylene

blocks.explanation: The catalyst family was expanded by Giulio Natta to create stereoregular polymers, such as crystalline polypropylene (Did You Know?).

book_ref.quote: This same catalyst family was expanded by Giulio Natta

blocks.prompt: 20 Plasticizers work by:

options.text: adding more chlorine to the chains
reducing the strong forces between polymer chains
making new covalent bonds between chains

blocks.explanation: Plasticizers reduce the strong forces between polymer chains, allowing the chains to move more freely (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: They cause this by reducing the strong forces between polymer chains

blocks.prompt: 21 Rigid PVC is naturally resistant to burning and self-extinguishing because of its:
blocks.explanation: Due to the chlorine atoms, rigid PVC is naturally resistant to burning and self-extinguishing (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Due to the chlorine atoms, it is naturally resistant to burning and self-extinguishing.

blocks.prompt: 22 Which statement is NOT true for rigid PVC?

options.text: It is a good electrical insulator
It is soft and bends easily

blocks.explanation: Rigid PVC (without plasticizers) is hard and stiff and does not bend easily; it is a good insulator and resists weathering (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Rigid PVC (without plasticizers) is hard and stiff and doesn't bend easily.

blocks.prompt: 23 Compared with rigid PVC, plasticised PVC:

options.text: is flexible and less rigid but keeps good chemical and electrical properties

blocks.explanation: Plasticised PVC is flexible and soft; it maintains good chemical and electrical properties, but is less rigid (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: It maintains good chemical and electrical properties, but is less rigid.

blocks.prompt: 24 PVC is used for water supply and sewage pipes because of its:
blocks.explanation: PVC pipes and fittings are used for water supply, drainage and sewage due to its corrosion resistance and durability (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Pipes and fittings for water supply, drainage, and sewage systems due to its corrosion resistance and durability.

blocks.prompt: 25 Which of the following is a medical use of PVC given in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: PVC is used for tubing, blood bags and catheters (Industrial Applications of PVC, 26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Tubing, blood bags, and catheters.

blocks.prompt: 26 Raincoats, artificial leather and inflatable swimming pools are listed as uses of:
blocks.explanation: Raincoats, artificial leather and inflatable products are among the uses of PVC (26.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Raincoats, artificial leather, inflatable products (e.g., swimming pools).

blocks.prompt: 27 In condensation polymerisation, each time a new bond forms:

options.text: a double bond opens up with no loss

blocks.explanation: In condensation polymerisation, each time a new bond forms a small molecule is eliminated from the monomers (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: each time a new bond forms, a small molecule is eliminated from the monomers

blocks.prompt: 28 Which of the following is NOT listed as a small molecule eliminated in condensation polymerisation?
blocks.explanation: The small molecule is usually water, and can also be HCl, CH₃OH or NH₃; CO₂ is not listed (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: This small molecule is usually water can also be H₂O, HCl or CH₃OH, or NH₃.

blocks.prompt: 29 A monomer for condensation polymerisation must have:

options.text: at least two reactive functional groups
a chlorine atom on every carbon

blocks.explanation: Monomers must have at least two reactive functional groups (such as -OH, -COOH, -NH₂), placed on different ends (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Monomers must have at least two reactive functional groups (like -OH, -COOH, -NH₂) that can react with each other.

blocks.prompt: 30 Condensation polymerisation typically takes place:

options.text: by a free radical chain reaction

blocks.explanation: Condensation polymerisation typically happens in a step-by-step manner (Figure 26.3), unlike the chain reaction of addition (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: manner as depicted in Figure 26.3

blocks.prompt: 31 The linkage present in the backbone of a polyester is:
blocks.explanation: Polyesters have ester links [—C(=O)—O—] in their backbone (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Polyesters have ester links [—C(=O)—O—] in their backbone.

blocks.prompt: 32 The diol used in the preparation of Terylene (PET) is:
blocks.explanation: Terylene/PET is a polyester made from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Preparation of Terylene/PET, a polyester from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid

blocks.prompt: 33 Polyester is used as an alternative to cotton because of its:

options.text: low cost and ability to resist creases

blocks.explanation: Polyester is used as an alternative to cotton due to its low cost and ability to resist creases (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Polyester is used as an alternative to cotton due to its low cost and ability to resist creases.

blocks.prompt: 34 Polyesters are suitable for making fibres mainly because of their:
blocks.explanation: High tensile strength makes polyesters suitable to manufacture fibres (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Polyesters have special features, such as high tensile strength, which make them suitable to manufacture fibres.

blocks.prompt: 35 An example of a hard plastic in which polyester is used as cross links is:
blocks.explanation: Polyester is used as cross links to obtain hard plastics, e.g. glass fibre reinforced cross-linked polyester (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: An example is the glass fibre reinforced cross-linked polyester.

blocks.prompt: 36 The linkage present in the backbone of a polyamide is:
blocks.explanation: Polyamides have amide links [—C(=O)—NH—] in their backbone (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Polyamides have amide links [—C(=O)—NH—] in their backbone.

blocks.prompt: 37 Compared with dicarboxylic acids, dioyl chlorides are:
blocks.explanation: Dioyl chlorides (two -COCl groups) are more reactive than dicarboxylic acids (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Dioyl chlorides are more reactive than dicarboxylic acids.

blocks.prompt: 38 A dioyl chloride is a molecule with two:
blocks.explanation: A dioyl chloride is a molecule with two -COCl groups (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: a dioyl chloride (molecule with two -COCl groups)

blocks.prompt: 39 When n molecules of a diamine react with n molecules of a dicarboxylic acid, the number of water molecules released is:
blocks.explanation: Each repeat unit has two amide links and each link releases one water molecule, so n repeat units release 2n H₂O (Book correction, 26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Each repeat unit has two amide links and each link releases one small molecule

blocks.prompt: 40 An amino acid can form a polyamide on its own because it:

options.text: has both -NH₂ and -COOH groups in one molecule

blocks.explanation: An amino acid is a single monomer having both an -NH₂ group and a -COOH group in one molecule (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: An amino acid is a single monomer that has both an -NH₂ (amino) group and a -COOH (carboxylic acid) group in one molecule.

blocks.prompt: 41 The peptide bond formed between amino acids is a type of:
blocks.explanation: The -NH₂ of one amino acid reacts with the -COOH of another, removing water to form a peptide bond, which is a type of amide linkage (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Peptide bond is also a type of amide linkage.

blocks.prompt: 42 Proteins are:

options.text: natural polyamides made from amino acids

blocks.explanation: Proteins are natural polyamides made from amino acids (26.1.2; discussed in Chapter 27).

book_ref.quote: Proteins are natural polyamides made from amino acids

blocks.prompt: 43 The reaction of an acyl chloride with ammonia or an amine happens easily at room temperature because:

options.text: ammonia is a strong oxidising agent

blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides are fairly reactive, so the reaction with ammonia or an amine happens easily at room temperature (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: This reaction happens easily at room temperature because acyl chlorides are fairly reactive.

blocks.prompt: 44 The formula of methanamine, one of the amines named in the chapter, is:
blocks.explanation: Methanamine is CH₃-NH₂; (CH₃)₂NH is the other amine named with it (26.1.2).

book_ref.quote: methanamine (CH₃-NH₂), N, N-dimethylamine

blocks.prompt: 45 Nylon is a:
blocks.explanation: Nylon is a type of synthetic polyamide formed by condensation polymerisation (26.2).

book_ref.quote: Nylon is a type of synthetic polyamide.

blocks.prompt: 46 The correct systematic name of adipic acid, HOOC-(CH₂)₄-COOH, is:
blocks.explanation: Its two COOH carbons are C1 and C6, so it is hexanedioic acid (hexane-1,6-dioic acid); '1,4-hexanedioic acid' is a misprint (Book correction, 26.2).

book_ref.quote: Adipic acid, HOOC-(CH₂)₄-COOH, has its two COOH carbons at C1 and C6

blocks.prompt: 47 Nylon-6 is formed from the single monomer:
blocks.explanation: Nylon-6 is formed from a single monomer called caprolactam (26.2).

book_ref.quote: which is formed from a single monomer called caprolactam

blocks.prompt: 48 Nylon-6 gets its name because:

options.text: its monomer has six carbon atoms
it is made from six different monomers
each chain has six repeat units
it melts at six hundred degrees

blocks.explanation: It is named nylon-6 because it involves a monomer (caprolactam) with six carbon atoms (26.2).

book_ref.quote: It is named nylon-6 because it involves a monomer with six carbon atoms.

blocks.prompt: 49 The structure of caprolactam is:
blocks.explanation: Caprolactam has a cyclic structure (26.2).

book_ref.quote: Caprolactam has a cyclic structure as shown in the following figure.

blocks.prompt: 50 The formation of nylon-6 from caprolactam is not a typical condensation reaction because:
blocks.explanation: No small molecule is removed during the reaction, so it is not a typical condensation reaction (26.2).

book_ref.quote: The reaction is not a typical condensation reaction because no small molecule is removed during the reaction.

blocks.prompt: 51 Nylon-6 is still classified as a condensation polymer because of:

options.text: the opening of a C=C bond
the mode of formation of the amide linkage

blocks.explanation: Nylon-6 is classified as a condensation polymer due to the mode of formation of the amide linkage (26.2).

book_ref.quote: nylon 6 is classified as a condensation polymer due to the mode of formation of the amide linkage

blocks.prompt: 52 Nylon-6 is easier to mold than nylon-6,6 because:
blocks.explanation: Nylon-6 is easier to mold as its melting point is lower than that of nylon-6,6 (26.2).

book_ref.quote: It is easier to mold as its melting point is lower than nylon-6,6.

blocks.prompt: 53 Nylon-6 is mostly used in rollers, skateboard wheels and power tool handles in order to:
blocks.explanation: Nylon-6 provides a smoother surface and higher impact resistance, so it is used in rollers, skateboard wheels and tool handles to avoid shocks (26.2).

book_ref.quote: It is mostly used in rollers, skate board wheels, and power tool handles to avoid shocks.

blocks.prompt: 54 The slippery surface of nylon is useful because it:
blocks.explanation: Nylon has a slippery surface that reduces friction (26.2.1).

book_ref.quote: Slippery surface, reduces friction.

blocks.prompt: 55 Nylon is stretchable because of its:
blocks.explanation: Nylon is stretchable due to elasticity (26.2.1).

book_ref.quote: Stretchable due to elasticity.

blocks.prompt: 56 Nylon is generally resistant to:

options.text: water wear only in hot water

blocks.explanation: Nylon is generally resistant to oils, many solvents and alkalis, and has a high melting point (26.2.1).

book_ref.quote: Generally resistant to oils, many solvents, and alkalis.

blocks.prompt: 57 Nylon is used for gears, bearings, engine covers and fuel lines in the automotive industry due to its:

options.text: strength, low friction and heat resistance

blocks.explanation: Nylon is used for automotive parts due to its strength, low friction and heat resistance (26.2.2).

book_ref.quote: due to its strength, low friction, and heat resistance

blocks.prompt: 58 Which consumer goods are listed as made of nylon?
blocks.explanation: Zippers, toothbrushes, hairbrushes and various molded plastic parts are made of nylon (26.2.2).

book_ref.quote: Consumer goods like zippers, toothbrushes, hairbrushes, and various molded plastic parts are made of nylon.

blocks.prompt: 59 Nylon is used for screws, nuts and bolts where the requirement is:
blocks.explanation: Nylon makes machine parts such as screws, nuts and bolts where strength and wear resistance are needed (26.2.2).

book_ref.quote: screws, nuts, bolts, and various industrial components where strength and wear resistance are needed

blocks.text: 26.3 Identifying the Type, Repeat Unit and Monomers of a Polymer

blocks.prompt: 60 The first step in identifying the type of a polymer from its formula is to:

options.text: identify the atoms in its backbone (main chain)

blocks.explanation: First check what atoms make up the main horizontal chain, i.e. identify the backbone (26.3).

book_ref.quote: The first thing to check is what atoms make up the main horizontal chain of the polymer

blocks.prompt: 61 A polymer whose main chain consists only of carbon atoms is:
blocks.explanation: If the main chain consists only of carbon atoms, it is an addition polymer formed from alkenes (26.3).

book_ref.quote: If the main chain consists only of carbon atoms (-C-C-C-C-), it is an addition polymer.

blocks.prompt: 62 A polymer whose main chain contains O or N atoms along with carbon is:
blocks.explanation: If the main chain contains oxygen or nitrogen atoms with carbon, it is a condensation polymer, like polyesters or polyamides (26.3).

book_ref.quote: If the main chain contains oxygen (O) or nitrogen (N) atoms with carbon, it is a condensation polymer

blocks.prompt: 63 A polymer is classified as a polyester when its chain has:

options.text: a C=O group directly next to an N-H
a C=O group directly next to an oxygen atom
a C=C bond in every unit

blocks.explanation: If a carbonyl group (C=O) is directly attached next to an oxygen, the polymer is a polyester (26.3).

book_ref.quote: If a carbonyl group (C=O) is directly attached next to an oxygen (O).

blocks.prompt: 64 A C=O group directly next to an N carrying an H shows:

options.text: an ester linkage, so the polymer is a polyester
an amide (peptide) linkage, so the polymer is a polyamide

blocks.explanation: A carbonyl directly next to an N with an H attached is an amide or peptide linkage; the polymer is a polyamide such as nylon-6,6 or Kevlar (26.3).

book_ref.quote: it presents an amide or peptide linkage

blocks.prompt: 65 According to Table 26.1, PLA (poly(lactic acid)) is a:
blocks.explanation: Table 26.1 lists Terylene and PLA as polyesters (-COO- links) (26.3).

book_ref.quote: Terylene, PLA (poly(lactic acid))

blocks.prompt: 66 According to Table 26.1, which pair are aromatic polymers (benzene rings in the chain)?
blocks.explanation: Polymers with benzene rings in the chain are aromatic polymers, e.g. PET or Kevlar (Table 26.1).

book_ref.quote: Benzene rings in the chain

blocks.prompt: 67 PTFE is:

options.text: a condensation polymer with HF lost

blocks.explanation: The monomer is tetrafluoroethene, so PTFE is poly(tetrafluoroethene); Table 26.1 lists it with addition polymers (only C-C bonds in the chain) (Book correction, 26.3).

book_ref.quote: The monomer is tetrafluoroethene, so the polymer is poly(tetrafluoroethene), PTFE.

blocks.prompt: 68 The repeat unit of a polymer is shown by:

options.text: writing the whole chain without brackets
placing brackets around one recurring section and adding the subscript n
writing the monomer with a double bond

blocks.explanation: Place brackets around one recurring section and add the subscript n; the section in brackets is the repeat unit (26.3).

book_ref.quote: Place brackets around one of these recurring sections and add the subscript n.

blocks.prompt: 69 To find the monomer of an addition polymer from its repeat unit you:

options.text: add water and break the ester bond
change the C-C single bond back into a C=C double bond

blocks.explanation: For addition polymers, change the C-C single bond in the repeat unit back into a C=C double bond (26.3).

book_ref.quote: change the C-C single bond in the repeat unit back into a C=C double bond to find the monomer

blocks.prompt: 70 When finding the monomers of a condensation polymer, after breaking the ester or amide bond you add:

options.text: -H to the C=O side and -OH to the N side
-OH to the C=O side and -H to the O or N side
a C=C bond to both sides

blocks.explanation: Add water back: break the ester or amide bond, add -OH to the C=O side and -H to the O or N side (26.3).

book_ref.quote: Add -OH to the C=O side and -H to the O or N side as given below.

blocks.prompt: 71 A polymer section is -CH₂-CH(C₆H₅)-CH₂-CH(C₆H₅)-. Its monomer and type are:
blocks.explanation: The backbone has only carbon atoms, so it is an addition polymer; the repeat unit -CH₂-CH(C₆H₅)- with C-C changed to C=C gives CH₂=CH-C₆H₅, phenyl ethene (26.3, 26.4.1).

book_ref.quote: These are formed from alkenes.

blocks.prompt: 72 A polymer section is -NH-CH₂-CH₂-NH-CO-CH₂-CH₂-CO-NH-CH₂-CH₂-NH-CO-CH₂-CH₂-CO-. The linkage and type are:
blocks.explanation: The chain contains N; a C=O is directly next to N-H, so the linkage is amide and the polymer is a condensation polyamide. The sequence duplicates after -NH-CH₂-CH₂-NH-CO-CH₂-CH₂-CO-, the repeat unit (26.3).

book_ref.quote: To find the repeating pattern, look for where the sequence starts to duplicate itself.

blocks.prompt: 73 Phenyl ethene, a monomer for addition polymerisation, is also called:
blocks.explanation: Monomers with C=C bonds such as ethene, propene and phenyl ethene (styrene) undergo addition polymerisation (26.4.1).

book_ref.quote: The examples include ethene, propene, phenyl ethene (styrene)

blocks.prompt: 74 An example of an addition copolymer given in the chapter is the copolymer of ethene and:
blocks.explanation: Two different monomers having double bonds can copolymerise, e.g. ethene and propenoic acid (H₂C=CH-COOH) (26.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Such an example is a copolymer of ethene and propenoic acid (H₂C=CH-COOH).

blocks.prompt: 75 Addition polymerisation mostly gives:
blocks.explanation: Mostly homopolymers are formed through addition polymerisation; copolymers of two monomers with double bonds are sometimes made (26.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Mostly homopolymers are formed through the addition polymerization

blocks.prompt: 76 Lactic acid can form a condensation polymer by itself because:

options.text: it has a C=C double bond
both reacting functional groups exist in a single molecule
it reacts with a Ziegler-Natta catalyst

blocks.explanation: The two functional groups may exist in a single molecule, e.g. lactic acid, or in two different molecules as in nylon-6,6 (26.4.2).

book_ref.quote: The two functional group may exist in a single molecule (e.g. lactic acid)

blocks.prompt: 77 Monomers with COCl groups and monomers with OH groups give:
blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides (COCl) and alcohols (OH) give a polyester and HCl (26.4.2).

book_ref.quote: acyl chlorides (COCl) and alcohols (OH) (polyester and HCl).

blocks.prompt: 78 HOOC-CH₂-CH₂-COOH and HO-CH₂-CH₂-OH are mixed. The expected polymerisation, polymer and small molecule are:
blocks.explanation: Each monomer has two functional groups and there is no C=C, so condensation takes place; COOH + OH gives a polyester and H₂O (26.4.2).

book_ref.quote: When there are two functional groups available for the formation of a bond

blocks.prompt: 79 H₂N-(CH₂)₆-NH₂ reacts with a dioyl chloride ClOC-R-COCl. The products are:
blocks.explanation: Amine groups (NH₂) with acyl chloride groups (COCl) give a polyamide and HCl (26.4.2).

book_ref.quote: amine group (NH₂) and acyl chlorides (COCl) (polyamide and HCl)

blocks.prompt: 80 The most widely used polymeric material on the globe is:
blocks.explanation: Plastic such as poly(ethene) is the most widely used polymeric material on the globe (26.5).

book_ref.quote: Plastic, such as poly(ethene), is the most widely used polymeric material on the globe.

blocks.prompt: 81 Conventional polymers are called non-degradable because they:

options.text: are broken down by sunlight in a day
cannot be broken down into simpler, non-toxic compounds

blocks.explanation: Non-degradable means these polymers cannot be broken down into simpler, non-toxic compounds, so they persist in the environment (Book correction, 26.5).

book_ref.quote: Non-degradable means that these polymers cannot be broken down into simpler, non-toxic compounds

blocks.prompt: 82 Microplastics are:

options.text: tiny pieces formed when large pieces of non-degradable plastic break down

blocks.explanation: Over time, large pieces of non-degradable plastics break down into tiny pieces called microplastics, which spread into soil, water and air (26.5).

book_ref.quote: large pieces of non-degradable plastics break down into tiny pieces called microplastics

blocks.prompt: 83 Plastic waste harms marine animals mainly because they:

options.text: absorb it through their skin as nutrients
mistake it for food and can get tangled in it

blocks.explanation: Animals, especially marine life, mistake plastic waste for food, leading to choking, injuries or starvation, and can get tangled in it (26.5).

book_ref.quote: Animals (especially marine life) can mistake plastic waste for food

blocks.prompt: 84 Non-degradable plastics create a landfill problem because:

options.text: they do not decompose and take up huge space

blocks.explanation: They take up huge amounts of space in landfills because they do not decompose; as population grows, finding landfill space becomes difficult (26.5).

book_ref.quote: As population grows, finding space for more landfills becomes difficult.

blocks.prompt: 85 To cope with non-degradable plastics, scientists are developing:
blocks.explanation: This leads to the development of two major classes: biodegradable and photodegradable polymers (26.5).

book_ref.quote: This leads to the need for the development of two major classes of polymers biodegradable and photodegradable polymers.

blocks.prompt: 86 A biodegradable plastic is one that:

options.text: is naturally decomposed by microorganisms into simpler non-toxic compounds when buried

blocks.explanation: Biodegradable plastic is naturally decomposed by microorganisms into simpler non-toxic compounds when buried for a certain period (26.5.1).

book_ref.quote: naturally decomposed by microorganism into simpler non-toxic compounds

blocks.prompt: 87 Plastics containing starch degrade faster because:

options.text: soil bacteria can attack natural polymers easily
starch adds chlorine to the chain

blocks.explanation: Plastics containing natural polymers such as starch degrade faster because soil bacteria attack natural polymers easily (26.5.1).

blocks.prompt: 88 The polymer named in the chapter as enhancing the biodegradability of plastic is:
blocks.explanation: Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) can enhance the biodegradability of plastic (Figure 26.6, 26.5.1).

book_ref.quote: poly(lactic acid) (PLA) can enhance the biodegradability of plastic

blocks.prompt: 89 To enhance photoabsorption, some polymers have been developed with which group in their chains?
blocks.explanation: Some polymers with carbonyl groups (C=O) in their chains have been developed due to their enhanced photoabsorption (26.5.2).

blocks.prompt: 90 When a photodegradable polymer absorbs UV light:

options.text: bonds within the chain and forces between chains are weakened
new cross links make it harder

blocks.explanation: Absorption of UV light weakens the bonds within the chain and the forces between chains, making the polymer more biodegradable (26.5.2).

book_ref.quote: The absorption of the UV light weakens the bonds within the chain

blocks.prompt: 91 One limitation of photodegradable plastics is that:

options.text: in landfills they are buried where no light is available
they are too costly to make

blocks.explanation: Photodegradable plastics cannot be used for long, recycling them is not efficient, and in landfills no light is available (26.5.2).

book_ref.quote: the plastic is buried in landfills where no light is available for photodegradability

blocks.prompt: 92 Dissolvable stitches are made from:

options.text: polyesters that slowly break down in the body by hydrolysis

blocks.explanation: Some medical implants and dissolvable stitches are made from polyesters that slowly break down in the body through hydrolysis (26.5.2).

blocks.prompt: 93 Artificial organs are:

options.text: man-made devices that replace or support damaged or diseased body parts

blocks.explanation: Artificial organs are man-made devices designed to replace or support the function of damaged or diseased body parts (26.6).

book_ref.quote: These are man-made devices designed to replace or support the function of damaged or diseased body parts.

blocks.prompt: 94 A biocompatible polymer is one that:

options.text: does not harm the body, cause allergies or get rejected by the immune system

blocks.explanation: Polymers used in the body must not harm the body, cause allergies, or be rejected by the immune system (26.6).

book_ref.quote: They must not harm the body, cause allergies, or be rejected by the immune system.

blocks.prompt: 95 Polymers for artificial organs are called tunable because their:

options.text: strength, flexibility or elasticity can be adjusted to match the body part
melting point is always the same

blocks.explanation: Their strength, flexibility or elasticity can be adjusted to match the body part, e.g. flexible for blood vessels and strong for bones (26.6).

book_ref.quote: Their strength, flexibility, or elasticity can be adjusted to match the body part they replace

blocks.prompt: 96 Artificial blood vessels (grafts) are made from:

blocks.prompt: 97 Specialized polyurethanes and silicone are used for:
blocks.explanation: Artificial heart valves use specialized polyurethanes and silicone: highly flexible, durable and resistant to clotting (Table 26.2).

blocks.prompt: 98 UHMWPE is used for artificial hip and knee joints because it:

blocks.explanation: Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene provides a smooth, low-friction surface to allow movement and resist wear (Table 26.2).

blocks.prompt: 99 The polymer for an artificial cornea must be:
blocks.explanation: An artificial cornea, made from PMMA and hydrogels, must be perfectly clear and biocompatible to restore vision (Table 26.2).

blocks.prompt: 100 In artificial skin, collagen and PLA act as:

blocks.explanation: Collagen (natural) and PLA (synthetic) act as a scaffold for new skin growth; some dissolve as the wound heals (Table 26.2).
